content:
Hi all — while working through Formal Conjectures statements and proofs, I collected several cases where the current Lean statement appears to differ from the cited problem, or becomes vacuous/degenerate for a boundary case.

I would rather report these once than open a burst of individual issues. These are statement-audit findings, not claims that the intended mathematical problems have been solved. Please correct me if any of these formulations are intentional.

1. High-confidence source/statement mismatches

  • Optimization Constant C1a: the convolution supremum uses t ∈ [1/2,1], while the official definition uses t ∈ [-1/2,1/2]. With the current interval, a short indicator-function witness gives C1a = 0, affecting the solved bounds and the open variants.
  • Erdős 996: the Fourier sum is indexed by i but uses the fixed coefficient fourierCoeff f k; additionally, the hypothesis controls ‖Sₖ f‖₂ rather than the cited tail norm ‖f - Sₖ f‖₂. Existing solved variants inherit the shared definition.
  • Erdős 697: parts.i and parts.ii appear to have the two threshold assumptions reversed relative to the docstrings/source. Also, variants.delta_lt quantifies over m = 0, where the conclusion reduces to 0 < 0. All three are currently tagged research solved.
  • Erdős 887: in parts.i, the answer term is inside the binders for C and eventual n, so it can be instantiated with the left-hand side pointwise and closed by reflexivity; parts.ii has the intended single absolute constant. Separately, rosenfeld_4 quantifies an arbitrary ∃ C > 0 although the source fixes coefficient 1.
  • Erdős 918: the source asks about the fixed first infinite ordinal ω, but two statements bind ∀ (ω : Ordinal), producing a much stronger uniform scheme. These seem to need Ordinal.omega0 instead.
  • Erdős 1167: the module header records the source condition κ α > r, but the main theorem and two variants omit it. For r = 2, γ = 2, λ = ℵ₀, κ₀ = 𝔠, κ₁ = 2, the current premise holds while the conclusion is refuted by the constant coloring.
  • Erdős 757: IsAdmissible uses (B - B).ncard = 11, while the source and intake issue use 11 ≤ (B - B).ncard. Under the current equality definition the optimum changes, and the registered solved upper bound is false.
  • Green 72: the current eventual statement appears to assert that the extremal value is 2N, whereas the cited question asks whether 2N is eventually impossible. This looks like the direction has been reversed.

2. Degenerate boundary cases / vacuous wrappers

  • Erdős 940, large_integers quantifies over r ≥ 2; the intended range is r ≥ 3. At r = 2, the conclusion contradicts the solved density-zero theorem in the same file.
  • Erdős 694 assumes greatest/least elements of every totient fiber. The fiber over 3 is empty, so the hypotheses are inconsistent and the solved wrapper is vacuous. Restricting n to the image of φ would recover the intended content.
  • Erdős 939 has no positivity condition on the summands. Thus {0,1} handles r = 4, although the source problem concerns positive integers.
  • Green 21, fox_kleitman_modular includes k = 0. For k = 0, p = 2, the hypotheses are vacuous but the conclusion asks 0 ≠ 0; adding 0 < k seems intended.

3. Interpretation / answer semantics

  • Erdős 357, weak-monotone variant: the current HasDistinctSums compares singleton intervals, so repetitions are automatically forbidden and weak monotonicity collapses to strict monotonicity. The natural-language problem explicitly allows aᵢ = aⱼ; the Erdős Problems discussion also suggests not comparing distinct length-one intervals. I think this variant needs an interpretation decision before being marked solved.
  • Several answer statements can return the unknown target itself rather than determine it: for example Erdős 195 admits answer (sSup S) = sSup S by rfl, while Erdős 188 and Erdős 1047 can select an unknown least/greatest value classically. I do not think these should become individual solve PRs; perhaps they belong in one semantic-review issue.

4. Open-PR blockers

  • PR #4660 (Erdős 265): IsRationalPairSequence uses equalities involving tsum without Summable/HasSum. Since Mathlib totalizes a nonsummable tsum to 0, divergent series can satisfy the predicate with rational value 0.
  • PR #4866 (Boundary Vertex): there is no positive-dimensional/nontrivial-space assumption and no full-rank/discrete lattice condition. In the zero-dimensional one-point space, the premises can hold while the frontier conclusion fails.

Already tracked

  • Erdős 80: #4867
  • Erdős 319 answer/optimality issue: #4892
  • Erdős 769 status issue: #4806 — the additional observation is that n = 0 makes every IsCutoff 0 c impossible.

I have short witnesses and proposed statement fixes for each item, but I have not opened new individual issues for the list above. I am happy to leave this as a consolidated handoff, or split out only the items maintainers consider useful.

One caveat: this list was organized with AI assistance from my long working notes, so it may contain transcription or interpretation errors. Please treat these as triage leads rather than independently verified bug reports. Thanks!

Thanks @Kenta Kitamura! If you would like to avoid many individual issues (and these all fit a similar theme of misformalization), you could also make a tracking issue like this one so it's easier for us to coordinate the work on Github together
